rules.summary: BI-EUR is core class I, which the prospectus restricts to institutional investors. The prospectus defines these as investors under art. 174 of the 2010 Law: credit institutions and other financial professionals investing for themselves or for others (including retail clients under a discretionary management agreement), insurance companies, pension funds and other UCIs. CONTRADICTION: the BI-EUR KID says the fund 'is suitable for all types of investors through all distribution channels', which conflicts with the institutional-only rule. A validator must decide.

citations.quote: I Institutional investors. Yes None

institutional investors Investors within the meaning of article 174 of the 2010 Law, such as credit institutions and other financial professionals investing on the behalf of themselves or other investors (whether retail in connection with a discretionary management agreement or institutional), as well as insurance companies, pension funds, or other UCIs.
The fund is suitable for all types of investors through all distribution channels.

rules.summary: Shares may not be offered or sold in the USA, and US persons may not subscribe unless the board or management company decides otherwise. 'US person' is defined mainly by residence and place of organisation, plus any US person under Rule 902 of Regulation S. Anyone who is a 'Non-United States person' under CFTC Rule 4.7 is carved out. US taxpayers may subscribe if they are not US persons, so US citizenship alone does not exclude an investor.

citations.quote: The shares in the SICAV may not be directly or indirectly offered or sold in the USA. Unless otherwise decided by the board or the management company, US persons may not subscribe for shares in the SICAV.
Therefore, US taxpayers, as defined for US federal income tax purposes, may subscribe for shares in the SICAV as long as they do not qualify as US persons.
any other U.S. person defined by US Rule 902 of Regulation S
